newsitem.title: NORWAY: FORECAST-Norway's March CPI seen up 3.15 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Norway's March CPI seen up 3.15 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Norwegian consumer prices (CPI) are expected to rise in March by an average 3.15 percent compared with March 1996 and by 0.35 percent from February, according to a Reuter poll of 10 analysts.
Year-on-year estimates for inflation were in a range between 2.8 percent and 3.6 percent, while estimates for the month-on-month figure fell between 0.0 percent and 0.8 percent.
The analysts said uncertainty on inflation stemmed from gasoline and electricity prices and the effect that a strong crowns had had on import prices.
For the year, analysts forecast inflation at 2.5 percent compared with projections of 2.425 percent in a February survey.
Norway's CPI is due to be released on April 10 at 0745 GMT.

Participants in the survey were Bergen Fonds, Chase Manhatten Bank, Den Danske Bank, Fokus Bank, Fondspartner, Handelsbanken, I.D.E.A., Christiania og Kreditkasse, Orkla Finans and Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken.
